Led by Head of IT and VP Engineering.

- CISO job description posted; engage executive recruiter
- Executive sponsor confirmed (CEO or COO); program budget approved
- Draft ISMS scope refined and approved by leadership
- Select GRC tooling shortlist (Vanta, Drata, Secureframe, or Hyperproof); begin trials
- Kick off vendor inventory — list every supplier touching PHI or production
- Begin asset inventory consolidation (CMDB cleanup)
- Enforce MFA for all users (not just admins) — quick win, high value
- Extend SIEM log retention contract to 12 months minimum
- Engage ISO 27001 implementation consultant [CONTRACTOR] for 3–6 month part-time engagement

- Risk assessment methodology approved

# Months 0–3 Priorities and Contractor Recommendations

## 1) Top Remediation Priorities, Months 0–3

### a) Must-start-now: Head of IT and VP Engineering (before CISO arrives)

- **Enforce MFA for all users** (not just admins) across SSO, VPN, email, and cloud consoles. Fastest high-value win; no CISO needed.
- **Extend SIEM log retention to 12+ months** and inventory log sources. Any gap here delays audit evidence for a year.
- **Consolidate the asset inventory / CMDB**: every production system, cloud account, repo, and data store with an owner and a PHI flag.
- **Build the vendor inventory**: every supplier touching PHI or production, with current BAA status. This is the raw input the CISO will need on day one.
- **Select and start trials of a GRC platform** (Vanta, Drata, Secureframe, or Hyperproof). Pick on usability, not features; the CISO will live in it.
- **Deploy a vulnerability scanner** across cloud and endpoints (Wiz, Tenable, or Qualys). Start generating data even without SLAs yet.
- **Audit non-production environments for real PHI**. If found, remove or mask immediately — this is the highest regulatory risk you carry today.
- **Universal endpoint coverage check**: confirm EDR and disk encryption on 100% of endpoints; remediate gaps.
- **Engage an ISO 27001 implementation consultant** (part-time, 3–6 months) so policy drafting and methodology work can start before the CISO arrives.
- **Executive sponsor and budget locked in writing**, with the 11-month timeline communicated to the board.

### b) CISO leads immediately on arrival (end of month 2)

- **Approve risk assessment methodology** and run the first risk workshops with Head of IT, VP Eng, Legal, and Product.
- **Own the policy suite**: review consultant drafts, tailor to your context, drive leadership approval and publication.
- **Produce Statement of Applicability v1** across all 93 Annex A controls with justifications.
- **Finalize ISMS scope and context documentation**; get leadership sign-off on record.
- **Stand up the vendor risk program** with Legal and Procurement; approve the BAA template and tiering model.
- **Launch the security awareness program** (platform selection may be done; CISO owns rollout, training content, and phishing baseline).
- **Define security KPIs and the management review cadence**; schedule the first review for month 7.
- **Select PAM vendor and sign off on implementation partner scope** (groundwork done by Head of IT in month 1–2).
- **Establish the incident response program**: playbooks, on-call, forensics readiness, and an IR retainer decision.
- **Approve the internal audit plan** and select the independent internal auditor (contractor) for month 8.

---

## 2) Contractor Recommendations

### PAM (Privileged Access Management)

**Types of firms to engage**

- **PAM product vendors with professional services arms**: CyberArk, BeyondTrust, Delinea (formerly Thycotic), Keeper Security, Teleport, StrongDM. For cloud-heavy environments like yours, Teleport and StrongDM are often faster to deploy than CyberArk.
- **Boutique IAM/PAM implementation partners**: firms like Integral Partners, Idenhaus, SecurIT, or regional MSPs with named PAM practices. Prefer these over large consultancies for speed and cost.
- **Avoid** the Big 4 for the build phase unless you already have an MSA; they're overkill for this scope.

**3-month engagement scope**

- *Month 1 — Design*: discovery of all privileged accounts (human and service), tiering model (Tier 0/1/2), target architecture, break-glass design, integration plan with SSO and SIEM. Deliverable: PAM design document and rollout plan.
- *Month 2 — Deploy Tier 0*: production AWS root and admin accounts, domain admins, database superusers. Session recording and approval workflows live. Deliverable: Tier 0 vaulted with evidence.
- *Month 3 — Expand to Tier 1 and handover*: dev and ops admin roles, CI/CD service accounts, operational runbooks, admin training, break-glass test. Deliverable: Tier 1 vaulted, runbooks, trained internal admins, exit report.

**Rough cost ranges (year 1, your size)**

- **Tool licensing**: $40K–$120K per year depending on vendor and seat count. Teleport and StrongDM tend toward the lower end for cloud-native; CyberArk and BeyondTrust toward the higher end.
- **Implementation services**: $60K–$150K for a 3-month engagement (roughly $20K–$50K per month, 0.5–1.0 FTE from the partner).
- **Total year-1 budget to plan for**: **$100K–$270K**.

### Vendor Risk and BAA Program

**Types of firms to engage**

- **Healthcare-specialist law firms or boutiques**: for BAA template, HIPAA sub-contractor flow-down, state privacy clauses, and contractual review playbooks. Look for firms with a dedicated HIPAA or digital health practice (e.g., Nixon Gwilt, Hall Render, or healthcare partners at regional firms).
- **Third-party risk management (TPRM) specialists or security program consultants**: firms that design vendor risk programs end-to-end. Options include boutique GRC firms (e.g., Risk3sixty, TrustedSec's GRC practice, Schellman's advisory arm) or TPRM platform vendors with professional services (OneTrust, ProcessUnity, Prevalent, Whistic).
- **Optional: a HIPAA-specialist advisory firm** (e.g., Clearwater, Intraprise Health) if you want combined HIPAA and ISO alignment in one engagement. Often efficient for healthcare SaaS.

**3-month engagement scope**

- *Month 1 — Program design and legal foundation*: vendor tiering model (critical/high/medium/low based on PHI access and criticality), BAA template refresh, DPA template, security questionnaire set (SIG Lite or CAIQ-based), risk acceptance workflow, policy and procedure documents. Deliverables: approved program design, legal templates, questionnaires.
- *Month 2 — Tooling and top-tier assessment*: TPRM platform configured (if adopted) or lightweight workflow in GRC tool; assess top 20 vendors (those touching PHI first), remediate BAA gaps, document findings. Deliverables: 20 vendor assessments, updated BAAs, risk register entries.
- *Month 3 — Operationalization and handover*: ongoing cadence (annual reassessment for high-tier, event-driven reviews), onboarding checklist for new vendors, procurement integration, internal training for Procurement and Legal, metrics and reporting. Deliverables: runbook, trained team, first management review input.

**Rough cost ranges (year 1)**

- **Legal services**: $15K–$40K for BAA/DPA template work and playbook; more if deep contract renegotiation is needed.
- **TPRM/program design consulting**: $50K–$120K for a 3-month engagement.
- **TPRM platform licensing (optional)**: $20K–$60K per year at your size; you can defer this year one and run vendor assessments inside your GRC tool to save money.
- **Total year-1 budget to plan for**: **$65K–$220K**, lower end if you skip a dedicated TPRM platform and use your GRC tool.

---

**One handover note for the recruiter**: the CISO profile that fits this program is someone who has taken a healthcare or regulated SaaS org from zero to ISO 27001 certification before, ideally with HIPAA and HITRUST exposure. Builder-operator profile, not a pure strategist. Comfortable in AWS, hands-on with risk workshops, and willing to run the first internal audit cycle personally if needed.
